entries.headline: First Lithium Minerals raises $1.44 million across a LIFE offering and placement
entries.dek: The financing combined a Listed Issuer Financing Exemption offering with a private placement, pricing units from 11 to 15 cents to fund exploration in Chile and Ontario.
entries.caption: First Lithium Minerals raised $1.44 million combining a LIFE offering and private placement for its Chile and Ontario projects.

sources.title: First Lithium Minerals Announces Closing of Second Tranche of LIFE Offering and Private Placement for Gross Proceeds of $1,442,144
First Lithium Minerals Secures $1.44M in Second Tranche LIFE Offering and Private Placement

unverified_claims: First Lithium Minerals' description of its planned use of proceeds for exploration and corporate purposes is the company's own stated intention, not an independently confirmed allocation.
brief: First Lithium Minerals Corp. (CSE: FLM), which explores for lithium and alkali metals at the Salar de Ascotan in Chile and for gold and critical metals in northwestern Ontario, has closed the second tranche of its Listed Issuer Financing Exemption offering together with a concurrent private placement, raising a combined $1,442,144.

The LIFE tranche sold non-flow-through units at $0.11 and flow-through units at $0.15 for $597,345; the private placement sold units at $0.11 for $844,840. Every unit carries half a warrant exercisable at $0.18 for three years. The company paid cash finder's fees of $23,908 and $33,387 plus finder's warrants on the two offerings.

The private placement units carry the standard four-month-and-one-day hold; the LIFE units do not. First Lithium said net proceeds will fund exploration at both projects along with general corporate and working capital purposes.
body: First Lithium Minerals Corp. (CSE: FLM, OTC Pink: FLMCF, FSE: X28) explores for lithium and other alkali metals at the Salar de Ascotan in northern Chile, and for gold and critical metals at the Lidstone project in northwestern Ontario. The company said on October 29 that it has closed the second tranche of its Listed Issuer Financing Exemption, or LIFE, offering together with a concurrent private placement, for combined gross proceeds of $1,442,144.

The LIFE tranche raised $597,345 through 2,466,773 non-flow-through units at $0.11 per unit and 2,173,333 flow-through units at $0.15 per unit. A Listed Issuer Financing Exemption lets a company already listed on an exchange sell securities to the public without a prospectus, provided it meets disclosure conditions set by securities regulators.

The concurrent private placement raised a further $844,840 through 7,680,363 units at $0.11 per unit. Every unit across both offerings — LIFE and private placement alike — carries one-half of a common share purchase warrant, with a whole warrant exercisable at $0.18 per share for three years from closing.

The private placement units are subject to the standard statutory hold period of four months and one day from closing. The LIFE Offering units, consistent with the exemption's design, carry no such hold and are freely tradeable once issued.

First Lithium paid cash finder's fees of $23,908 plus 220,542 finder's warrants at $0.11 in connection with the LIFE tranche, and $33,387 in cash plus 337,702 finder's warrants in connection with the private placement.

The company said net proceeds will go toward exploration activities at its Chile and Ontario projects, along with general corporate purposes and working capital. The release, filed through Newsfile Corp. from Toronto, did not break out how the proceeds will be divided between the two projects.

entries.headline: Fuse Battery Metals closes $644,560 private placement at five cents a unit
entries.dek: The non-brokered deal priced units at five cents each, with insiders taking part and the financing still subject to TSX Venture Exchange approval.
entries.caption: Fuse Battery Metals closed a $644,560 private placement of 12.9 million units priced at five cents each.

sources.title: Fuse Battery Closes Non-Brokered Private Placement Financing

unverified_claims: Fuse Battery Metals' stated intention to use proceeds for 'strategic acquisition opportunities' and to 'evaluate potential transactions' is the company's own forward-looking description and not yet a specific transaction.
brief: Fuse Battery Metals Inc. (TSXV: FUSE), which holds cobalt properties near Cobalt, Ontario, has closed a non-brokered private placement of 12,891,200 units at $0.05 per unit, raising gross proceeds of $644,560. Each unit comprises one common share and one warrant.

Each warrant lets the holder buy one additional share at $0.05 for five years from closing. Insiders subscribed for 272,040 of the units, worth $13,602, and the company issued 30,000 common shares at a deemed $0.05 as a finder's fee. The placement still needs final TSX Venture Exchange acceptance.

All securities are subject to a statutory hold period expiring March 2, 2027. Fuse said it will use the proceeds to pursue strategic acquisition opportunities, evaluate potential transactions, and support ongoing corporate operations, working capital requirements and future business initiatives.
body: Fuse Battery Metals Inc. (TSXV: FUSE, OTC: FSBMF, FRA: 43W3) is a Canadian exploration company focused on metals used in battery manufacturing, including cobalt properties near Cobalt, Ontario. The company said on October 29 that it has closed a non-brokered private placement of 12,891,200 units at $0.05 per unit, for gross proceeds of $644,560.

Each unit consists of one common share and one common share purchase warrant, with each warrant exercisable at $0.05 per share for five years from closing. Insiders of the company subscribed for 272,040 of the units in the placement, representing gross proceeds of $13,602.

In connection with the financing, Fuse issued 30,000 common shares at a deemed value of $0.05 per share as a finder's fee. All securities issued under the private placement, including the finder's shares, are subject to a statutory hold period expiring March 2, 2027 under applicable Canadian securities laws.

The private placement remains subject to final acceptance by the TSX Venture Exchange. Fuse said it intends to use the proceeds to pursue strategic acquisition opportunities, evaluate potential transactions, and support its ongoing corporate operations, working capital requirements and future business initiatives.

The release noted that more than CAD$25 million has been spent to date — stated in 2020 dollars, inflation-adjusted — on the company's Teledyne Property, one of the cobalt holdings the financing is intended to support alongside the company's other corporate purposes.

Beyond the financing terms and the brief reference to the Teledyne Property, the release gave no further operational update — no drill results, property description or revised budget — so this entry is limited to what the release discloses.
